extracted.intended_audience: aspiring fiction writers, especially those facing rejection or preparing a debut novel
extracted.subtask_description: Advice and personal reflections on persisting as a fiction writer through rejection, revising a novel, and retaining artistic integrity; aimed at writers working toward publication or craft improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Begin writing from images
rubrics_metrics.description: I start most of my writing with images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use vivid images as an entry point to scenes and drafts — concrete sensory starting points can ground work and restore momentum when other elements feel unsettled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write even in times of personal disorientation
rubrics_metrics.description: Sit down to write during times of disorientation and frailty rather than stopping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writing in difficult periods can restore a 'non-shame' and offer psychological repair; the author describes returning to a small table and using the act of writing to cope with life upheaval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use short forms to restore confidence
rubrics_metrics.description: When a large project feels stalled or shaming, start a short story to restore writerly nerve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shifting to a shorter, more contained project can renew confidence and reinvigorate your practice without abandoning longer work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revise conscientiously for structure and pacing
rubrics_metrics.description: Take passes on the manuscript focused on structure and pacing, using editorial comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate generous editor feedback to improve architecture of the work; targeted revision passes (structure, pacing) are concrete actions that improve a draft's readiness for submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persist in submitting despite repeated rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Continued agent queries and slush submissions even when they seem to go nowhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat submission as a sustained activity; many rejections do not reflect absolute lack of quality — persistence keeps the work in circulation and increases chances of discovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write primarily for yourself, not for publication
rubrics_metrics.description: I understood that I would write for myself, without the prospect of publication; publishing is a business separate from writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize personal artistic goals and integrity over market trends. This stance helps maintain motivation and produces work truer to the writer's vision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain authenticity and keep yourself as highest critic
rubrics_metrics.description: Remain yourself as the highest critic and do not alter core elements to chase marketability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve your voice, central stylistic choices, and the elements that make your work distinct; editors/publishers may respond to authenticity rather than market-driven compromises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value craft and the creative process above external validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Craft and art matter above all else; love the hair-pulling, nail-biting process of creating prose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Find reward in the labor of writing itself; valuing craft sustains practice through rejection and long development periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage with the literature you want to be in conversation with
rubrics_metrics.description: Sit down in front of the literature I hoped to be in conversation with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surround yourself with work you admire and use it as a benchmark and source of conversation; reading widely and intentionally informs and elevates your own writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use editorial feedback selectively
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepted helpful comments from a generous former editor but did not change core elements of the novel to make it 'of-the-moment.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate constructive feedback that improves craft (structure, pacing, clarity) while resisting suggestions that would compromise the work's essential voice or aims for market trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow time and maturity to shape the work
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishing later in life produced a better novel — an earlier version 'would have been a lesser craft.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that development, life experience, and time spent revising can materially improve your work; do not rush publication if more growth is needed.
